finding: The tempting P=Q shortcut would identify the automatically bounded normalized B† with the required normalized B by adjunction. It is VACUOUS for every original Stiefel pair: Lambda is invertible, so P=Q implies p=Gamma(P)=Gamma(Q)=q. But pq=0, p²=p and Tr p=1, so p=q implies p=0, a contradiction.
second_finding: The shortcuts B=B† and B=-B† are also VACUOUS. Gamma preserves adjoints, so either would make x=Gamma(B) Hermitian or skew-Hermitian. The original matrix-unit equations imply x=p x q and pq=0, hence x²=0. In either case x†x=±x²=0, contradicting x†x=q and Tr q=1. This does not assert that general normal B is impossible, because Gamma is not a multiplicative map.
scope: Exact all-variable written algebra on the original d4 paired-column domain. No selected state, numerical trial, physical instance, parametric threshold, or held guide is used.
nonclaims: Not a q3 counterexample or a proof of the desired contraction; it rules out only equal diagonal outputs and Hermitian/skew-Hermitian cross blocks for original orthonormal pairs. It does not rule out general normal B, commutation, approximate relations, or other analytic routes. No novelty, formal proof, parent adoption or independent family review is claimed.
